for a university software engineering team.

using the search_style_guide action. Do not invent or assume style-guide rules.

At every step, respond with exactly one JSON object:

  "thought": "A short explanation of your next step",

Do not use Markdown fences or text outside the JSON object.

Use image placeholders such as {{image:aniket.jpg}}.
Never generate Base64 image data yourself.

After writing the website, inspect the complete checker report.
Fix every failing check and write the website again.
Only call finish when the full checker reports success.

{
  "profile_directory": "task1_opencode\content\content",
  "image_directory": "task1_opencode\content\content\images",
  "profiles": [
    {
      "filename": "aniket.md",
      "content": "# Aniket

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University, Germany. Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering from Savitribai Phule Pune University, India.

## Interests
Travelling, cooking, working out, gaming, dancing, painting and exploring new technologies.

## Fun fact
I once performed in a theatre skit and won an award at the Asia-level national competition.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI has made software development faster and more accessible, especially for debugging, learning and generating code. However, it can still produce incorrect solutions, so developers need to understand and verify what it generates. I see AI as a helpful assistant rather than a replacement for software engineering knowledge.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI agents will handle more routine coding, testing and debugging tasks. Software engineers will increasingly focus on system design, problem-solving, architecture and supervising AI-generated solutions. Understanding how to work effectively with AI will become an important developer skill.

## My hot take on AI
AI won't replace developers, but developers who use AI effectively may replace those who don't.
"
    },
    {
      "filename": "dheeraj.md",
      "content": "# Dheeraj

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University. Previously completed my B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering at Anurag University, India.

## Interests
Software development, gaming and anime, fitness.

## Fun fact
I helped organise a university hackathon that attracted over 800 participants!

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI has become a powerful tool for accelerating software development, from code generation and debugging to testing and documentation. However, it can also produce convincing but incorrect solutions, so understanding the underlying concepts and being able to critically evaluate its output are more important than ever.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Software engineering will likely become increasingly AI-assisted, with developers spending less time writing repetitive code and more time on architecture, problem-solving and system design. AI agents may independently handle entire development tasks, but human judgment, creativity and accountability will remain essential.

## My hot take on AI
The best software engineers of the future won't be those who write the most code, but those who know what code shouldn't be written.
"
    },
    {
      "filename": "guru_akaash.md",
      "content": "# Guru Akaash

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st Semester, University of Paderborn, Germany. Previously completed my B.E. in Computer Engineering, University of Mumbai, India in 2023.

## Interests
Software Development, Piano, Music, Table Tennis, exploring new places, and learning cooking.

## Fun fact
Worked on platforms that currently serve 700,000+ users and 1 million+ groups, won multiple national-level project hackathons and competitions, and secured a $15,000 Microsoft AI for Earth grant.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
The best software engineers of tomorrow won't necessarily be those who write the most code. They'll be those who understand problems deeply, make sound engineering decisions, and know how to leverage AI without blindly depending on it.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I believe there will be huge transformations over the next 5–10 years. Software engineering will not disappear; rather, the definition of what it means to be a software engineer will fundamentally change. The focus will shift from writing code to engineering systems, with software architecture and security becoming increasingly important. There will also be many new things for us to learn and apply in our day-to-day work.

## My hot take on AI
Use AI to amplify your engineering capabilities, not outsource your engineering thinking.
"
    },
    {
      "filename": "srivallabh.md",
      "content": "# Srivallabh

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester.

## Interests
Formula 1, auto journalism, cricket.

## Fun fact
I slept for 20 hours one day.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I think AI has changed software engineering quite a bit in the last couple of years. From my experience as a full-stack developer between 2024 and 2026, it made development much easier and faster. Things like debugging, writing boilerplate code, understanding unfamiliar codebases, exploring new technologies, and implementing features became significantly less time-consuming. I personally use LLMs as part of my regular development workflow, and they have become almost like another developer to discuss problems and solutions with.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think software engineering will become much more AI-driven in the next 5–10 years. Developers will spend less time writing code manually and more time defining problems, designing systems, reviewing AI-generated code, and making architectural decisions. AI agents might handle entire development tasks, from understanding requirements to implementation, testing, and deployment, with developers supervising the process.

## My hot take on AI
AI is making coding easier, but knowing what not to let AI do is becoming the real skill.
"
    },
    {
      "filename": "yashas.md",
      "content": "# Yashas

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, B.Tech in CS in AIML from Reva University.

## Interests
Machine Learning, Distributed Systems, Coding.

## Fun fact
I cook food for people.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI today acts as a powerful pair programmer that accelerates boilerplate generation and debugging, but it still lacks deep architectural context. It is incredibly useful for scaffolding projects, yet it requires constant oversight to ensure code security and maintainability. We are currently in a phase where AI augments human developers rather than replacing them, shifting the daily focus from syntax memorization to higher-level system design.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
The role of a software engineer will transition from writing raw code to orchestrating complex, AI-driven microservices and agents. Natural language will become a primary compilation step, with developers spending more time defining constraints, evaluating security, and managing cloud architectures. Traditional coding will still exist for performance-critical systems, but the vast majority of application development will be highly abstracted and automated.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is a temporary fad that will vanish once models actually learn to understand human intent.
"
    }
  ],
  "available_images": [
    "aniket.jpg",
    "dheeraj.jpg",
    "guru_akaash.jpg",
    "srivallabh.jpg",
    "yashas.jpg"
  ]
}
